Prepared transfer, rescoped by the captain on 2026-10-09. This acceptance replaces the clone delegation of pins v8 and v9.

Why the rescope. Seven review rounds (pins v5 to v9) tried to make firstmate reproduce Git's own choice of SSH program and SSH options for a clone. Each round found one more corner where firstmate's copy differed from Git: a copied config.worktree, an include chain exactly 10 levels deep, includeIf onbranch, and finally protocol version 0 with the default port, where Git hands ssh, simple, plink and putty the same arguments. These corners do not occur in this project's own use. The captain chose to let Git decide clones by itself and to keep firstmate's time limits only for fetch, push and ls-remote.

Fetch, push and ls-remote. The named boundary resolves the SSH command for each call, as acceptance 10 describes, and gives it to Git only through the child process's own environment: GIT_SSH_COMMAND points at the existing helper bin/lib/fm-ssh-transfer.sh, and the helper runs the resolved command with Git's arguments unchanged. The helper keeps Git's shell-command rules, so quoted identities still work. Nothing is written to a persistent or global setting, and no credential or configuration text goes into logs or board records. Ordinary raw operator git is not overridden.

Time limits on fetch, push and ls-remote. The approved limits are three OpenSSH options: ConnectTimeout=20, ServerAliveInterval=15 and ServerAliveCountMax=4. Preparation adds them only when the resolved SSH variant is ssh, which means OpenSSH. The variant counts as ssh when GIT_SSH_VARIANT is ssh; or, with GIT_SSH_VARIANT unset, when ssh.variant is configured as ssh; or, with both unset or set to auto, when the program name of the resolved command is ssh (ssh.exe counts). For every other variant (simple, plink, putty, tortoiseplink) and for an unrecognized program name that Git would probe with -G, preparation adds no options, because those programs reject OpenSSH options. Today bin/lib/fm_git_transfer.py prepare() adds the options whatever the variant is; that is the bug this fixes. Preparation still sets GIT_SSH_VARIANT from the resolved configuration or the recognized program name, as it does now, so Git and the helper agree on the variant.

Clone. firstmate does not wrap the SSH transport of git clone. For a clone, the named boundary does only two things: it removes firstmate's own generated GIT_SSH_COMMAND (the value that equals FM_SSH_GENERATED_COMMAND) from the clone's child environment, and it removes firstmate's internal FM_SSH_ variables from that environment. It then runs Git with the clone arguments unchanged. An operator's own GIT_SSH_COMMAND or GIT_SSH passes through unchanged, exactly as configuration sourcing left it. Git itself then reads every configuration layer, applies ssh.variant and starts the transport, exactly as for a clone the operator types. For a clone, preparation reads no configuration, creates no repository, configuration file or alias, and never writes, removes or creates the destination. Clone callers still go through the named boundary, because a raw git clone would otherwise inherit the generated helper command and fail. Unknown or malformed Git prefix options still fail closed, as for every other network call.

Accepted tradeoff, in plain words. A clone gets no firstmate timeout or keepalive. If the remote stops answering, the clone waits until SSH itself or the operator gives up. design §12 says this next to the network time limits (acceptance 6).

Keep or add these rows, each with a real Git process and local SSH stubs, and no real network:
1. A clone through the named boundary over a local upload-pack stub, with no operator override, succeeds. The transport receives Git's own argument list with no firstmate options, and the clone's child environment contains no GIT_SSH_COMMAND, no GIT_SSH set by firstmate and no FM_SSH_ variable.
2. The same clone with an operator GIT_SSH, and again with an operator GIT_SSH_COMMAND: the program the operator named receives Git's arguments, and the operator variable reaches Git unchanged.
3. Fetch and push with a resolved ssh variant (default ssh, configured ssh.variant=ssh, GIT_SSH_VARIANT=ssh) receive the three options. With ssh.variant simple, plink, putty and tortoiseplink, and with an unrecognized program under auto, they receive none.
4. The parent environment and the frozen code snapshot do not change.
